summary.headline: Sell practical cyber-readiness help to UK SMEs, with automation retainers as the recurring follow-on.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized cyber-hygiene and evidence-pack service for small UK businesses.
summary.why_now: The UK government's 2025 survey found 43% of businesses reported a cyber breach or attack in the previous 12 months; phishing remained the leading breach type. This supports a real pain signal, though it does not prove willingness to buy a solo consultancy.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene and readiness service
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope setup of MFA, backups, staff phishing basics, asset/account checklist and an evidence pack; refer or partner for regulated testing rather than claiming certification.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK's 2025 survey reports breaches/attacks at 43% of businesses and phishing in 85% of affected businesses. Buyers may need straightforward help translating guidance into action.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local professional-services firms, small agencies and suppliers asked security questions by larger customers.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£800 for basic tooling, insurance and outreach; exclude specialist testing/certification costs.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold through direct outreach and local IT/accountancy referrals; estimate, not guaranteed.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly/quarterly check-ins, staff onboarding and backup/MFA reviews; validate willingness to retain.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a software engineer comfortable with cloud identity, scripting and clear documentation; avoid representing as a certified auditor.
risks: Liability and trust barriers; scope and insurance need careful handling.
Survey prevalence is not evidence that microbusinesses will pay this provider or price.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best first test: sell a small, bounded implementation service before building software.

top_opportunities.name: SME workflow automation sprint
top_opportunities.description: Automate one repetitive admin workflow (lead intake, quote follow-up, invoice reminders or reporting) using the client's existing tools, with handover and support.
top_opportunities.why_now: A concrete time-saving project can be scoped and sold faster than a generic AI product; demand and pricing require local customer validation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades, recruiters, accountants and small B2B service firms with spreadsheet-heavy processes.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 using existing APIs and low-cost automation tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–4 weeks via paid discovery and a fixed-price pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monitoring, small improvements and support retainer.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong engineering fit; part-time delivery possible when tightly scoped.
risks: Integrations and client data quality can expand scope.
Generic AI automation is crowded; must sell a measurable workflow outcome.
top_opportunities.verdict: Good alternative when the founder has access to a specific vertical and workflow.

top_opportunities.name: Managed website care and conversion fixes
top_opportunities.description: Maintain, secure and improve existing local-business websites; bundle backups, updates, uptime checks, small edits and lead-form testing.
top_opportunities.why_now: A simple service with clear recurring maintenance can be sold locally; no fresh market-wide demand evidence was established in this run.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local trades, clinics and professional firms with dated or neglected websites.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 for monitoring, backups, hosting and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks by auditing prospects and offering a paid cleanup.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly maintenance plans plus separately priced improvements.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong if experienced in web delivery and client communication.
risks: Low-cost providers and DIY platforms create price pressure.
Support expectations can become unbounded without a service limit.
top_opportunities.verdict: Practical cash-flow service; differentiate on reliability and measurable enquiries, not redesign alone.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical lead follow-up and booking automation
top_opportunities.description: Install a compliant enquiry capture, rapid-response and appointment reminder workflow for one local service niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: Missed enquiries are a plausible operational problem, but this run found no independently verified current demand measure; validate with owner interviews.
top_opportunities.buyer: High-value appointment businesses such as specialist repair firms or private clinics.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for messaging/CRM tools and a demonstration workflow.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–4 weeks if a niche and buyer access are already available.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly workflow support and reporting; usage costs passed through transparently.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong technical fit; sales and privacy-safe implementation are essential.
risks: Consent, data protection and messaging rules must be handled correctly.
Reliance on third-party platforms and weak client follow-through can impair results.
top_opportunities.verdict: Promising only after confirming a costly missed-lead problem in one niche.

top_opportunities.name: Niche compliance evidence tracker micro-SaaS
top_opportunities.description: A narrowly focused checklist, reminders and evidence repository for one small-business procurement or policy workflow; start concierge-first.
top_opportunities.why_now: The cyber survey identifies a broad readiness gap, but it does not establish demand for a new tool; a paid manual pilot should precede product work.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small suppliers repeatedly answering security questionnaires or maintaining customer-required evidence.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,500 for a minimal hosted prototype and basic legal/security review.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Typically slower, 4–12+ weeks; faster only with pre-sold design partners.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Potential subscription if evidence and reminders are used continuously.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong build fit, but distribution and trust are substantial challenges.
risks: Longer sales cycle and crowded compliance software market.
Building before finding repeated paid pain can waste the budget.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build yet; seek three paid concierge pilots first.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene and readiness service
best_pick.why_it_wins: It combines a current official UK risk signal with a low-cost, bounded service that can earn before software is built. Start with implementation, keep claims conservative, and add recurring reviews only if customers value them.
validation_plan: Contact 20 local firms and referral partners; ask what security evidence customers request and what remains incomplete.
Offer three paid, fixed-scope readiness sessions; record conversion, delivery hours and requested follow-on support before standardising the offer.
best_pick.first_offer: A fixed-fee 90-minute security basics review plus written action list and one agreed improvement, priced after short discovery; no certification or penetration-test claims.
best_pick.mvp: Manual checklist, documented scope, secure customer handover and a lightweight reminder/review process; no custom SaaS initially.
customer_types: Local suppliers seeking to satisfy larger customers' security questions
best_pick.do_today: Use the GOV.UK survey as an opening conversation, identify 20 nearby prospects, and book discovery calls; do not buy tooling until a buyer commits.
